The area of a square is increasing. Find the instantaneous rate at which the area of a square is increasing with respect to the length of its side at the moment when the length of the sides is equal to $l=6\,\text{cm}.$
worked_solution:
We know that the area of the square with respect to $l$ is given by  

$$
A=A(l)={l}^{2}.
$$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $A(l)$  with respect to $l$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(l) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}l}({l}^{2})=2l,\end{aligned}
$$

and evaluating at $l=6$ gives

$$
{A}^{′}(6)=2(6)=12.
$$

 

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the area of the square is increasing when the length of the side is $l=6\,\text{cm}$ is $12\,{\text{cm}}^{2}/\text{cm}.$
